A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 Section 8 reports original synthetic sequence-modeling, structural-distillation and real-world language-modeling experiments, including Figures 5–8 and Tables 1–2.

after.justification: v3 retains these experiments in Section 7 and Appendix G and adds Standard MoE and billion-parameter model comparisons in Section 7.4.

M1.justification: The normalized input-dependent gate, frozen experts, primal-dual optimization, sampling procedures and cached-logit structural distillation are retained. Larger experimental model configurations and expanded explanations do not introduce a new proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate contradictory synthetic sequence rules, their overlapping mixtures, and Wikipedia, the-stack-smol and FineWeb-Edu text. v3 expands model scale without identifying additional datasets, tasks or input conditions.

E2.justification: v3 adds Standard MoE (Scratch) to the real-world comparison in Table 1: a capacity-matched model with shared attention and three routed feed-forward experts. The previous expert, monolithic and synthetic oracle comparators remain.

E3.justification: Beyond the retained approximately 20M-parameter experiment, v3 Section 7.4 adds three approximately 1.6B-parameter experts, a 2.5M-parameter gate and a 4.9B-parameter monolithic comparator. This substantially extends the evaluated model configurations. Existing synthetic and small-scale real-world settings are retained.

E4.justification: The domain-overlap tests, convergence observations, distillation comparison and real-world distribution-shift analysis are retained. v1 Figures 6–7 become v3 Figures 9–10, and Table 2 moves to Appendix G.4. The added scale and comparator results do not introduce a distinct ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Five-run averaging, variation across initialization seeds and data splits, and standard-deviation shading remain documented. Additional results use uncertainty notation without establishing a new reporting procedure or increased run count. The new estimator-variance argument is theoretical analysis.

E6.justification: v3 Table 1 adds MoE NLLs of 5.080 ± 0.009 and 5.245 ± 0.269. Section 7.4 newly reports large-model NLLs of 4.734 ± 0.006 for the gate and 4.829 ± 0.012 for the monolithic comparator. Synthetic curves also change between v1 Figure 5 and v3 Figure 4. Existing real-world table entries remain unchanged; the large-model results are additional settings, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v3 adds Proposition D.2 and its equality-condition proof, Proposition D.3 and its overlap-entropy lower-bound derivation, and the resulting monolithic-risk bound. Appendix F.3 also adds an O(p/|B|) partition-estimator variance argument. These extend the theory beyond the substantial relocation of existing proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims about robust gating, gate-complexity generalization, the JSD comparison, scalable optimization and structural distillation. New experiments support the existing scope rather than redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds explicit retraining-versus-gating applicability scenarios and substantive interpretations of equality and overlap. Section 7.4 adds explanations involving shared-layer interference in MoE and code-domain variability. Conversely, v1 Appendix C's discussion of bound tightness versus interpretability is removed.

D1.justification: v3 supplies architectural details for the new MoE comparator and large-model experiment, including 48-layer experts and comparator, embedding dimensions of 1600 and 2832, and gate size. Existing implementation details and hyperparameters are mostly retained elsewhere; the additions do not provide a complete separate large-model training recipe.

R1.justification: v3 adds numerous H-consistency references in Appendix A.1 and supporting citations for saddle-point dynamics and generalization, while removing the explicit Sagawa et al. (2020) DRO reference. The substantive positioning against source adaptation, routing, model merging and jointly trained MoE remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The long-form exposition becomes a condensed main paper with proof sketches and extensive reorganized appendices. Related work, proofs, algorithms, implementation details and several experiments move or are summarized. An appendix contents list and an impact statement are added.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main-paper layout and extensively resizes and relocates figures and tables. Main experimental plots receive revised legends, tick displays and shorter captions. Table 1 gains a MoE row and revised formatting; Table 2 and overlap figures move to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful MoE and large-model comparisons absent from v1, together with explicit equality and overlap analyses. However, the large-model experiment is sparsely documented, and new Appendix D.2.3 interpretations infer a greater gating advantage from a monolithic lower bound that does not establish that comparison. These evidential gains coexist with added overinterpretation of central theory, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
